title: Thine Arm, O Lord, in Days of Old
alsoKnownAs: Your Hand, O Lord, in Days of Old
description: Thine Arm, O Lord, in Days of Old in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 3 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Edward Hayes Plumptre. The tune, KINGSFOLD, is Traditional English. This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Thine_ arm, O Lord, in days of old, was_ strong to heal and_ save; It_ tri-umphed o'er di-sease and death, o'er_ dark-ness and_ the grave. To_ Thee they went,_ the blind, the dumb, the_ pal-sied_ and the lame, The_ le-per with_ his_ taint-ed life, the_ sick with fe_-vered frame.

lines: Thine arm, O Lord, in days of old,
was strong to heal and save;
It triumphed o'er disease and death,
o'er darkness and the grave.
To Thee they went, the blind, the dumb,
the palsied and the lame,
The leper with his tainted life,
the sick with fevered frame.
And lo! Thy touch brought life and health,
gave speech, and strength and sight;
And youth renewed and fear relieved
owned Thee, the Lord of light;
And now, O Lord, be near to bless,
Almighty as of yore,
In crowded street, by restless couch,
as by Gennesaret's shore.
Be Thou our great Deliverer still,
Thou Lord of life and death;
Restore and quicken, soothe and bless,
with Thine almighty breath.
To hands that work and eyes that see,
give wisdom's heavenly lore,
That whole and sick, and weak and strong,
may praise Thee evermore.
